subject: Post-call next steps — confidential logs, locality & TTL
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhou <emma@labsignal.ai>, Ravi Patel <legal@labsignal.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call next steps — confidential logs, locality & TTL

Hi Emma / Ravi — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of asks from your side:
- PII must never be persisted beyond request processing unless explicitly allowed by you.
- Storage locality: EU-only for any retained logs or telemetry.
- A way to provide “sample logs” for your security team without exposing full payloads.
- Option for a 0-retention mode for sensitive endpoints; fallback to short-term logs for troubleshooting when enabled.

What Redwood can offer (proposal):
1) Default behavior: masked transaction logs + structured telemetry retained for 7 days (EU-only). Masking covers user identifiers and any fields you flag.
2) 0-retention mode: for selected routes we can enforce ephemeral processing where no request/response payloads are written to disk (KV cache and transient memory only). We’d still keep non-PII telemetry (error counts, latency histograms).
3) Short-term debug window: with an explicit mutual action step (signed DPA addendum + temporary authorization), we can retain full logs for up to 48 hours for triage; logs are accessible only to named engineers and are deleted automatically.
4) Sample logs: send us a small anonymized sample (you offered to produce) and we’ll run the redaction pass and return a sanitized example and a redaction report.

Requested next steps:
- Emma/Ravi: share the anonymized sample logs you referenced and note the fields you must protect (PII list).
- Redwood (Marissa + Karthik): prepare a short DPA addendum draft for short-term debug windows and an EU-only hosting confirmation note.
- Legal sync: if acceptable, schedule a 30-min call next week to resolve the DPA wording.

I attached a short note outlining the three retention modes and EU residency confirmations. Opening for questions — I’ll follow up with a Doodle for the legal sync unless you prefer specific slots.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf (summary PDF, 3 pages)
From: Emma Zhou <emma@labsignal.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Patel <legal@labsignal.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T08:37:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call next steps — confidential logs, locality & TTL

Karthik — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) The default 7-day masked logs sound ok for general telemetry, but we need an explicit guarantee that any PII fields (email, national ID, phone) are never written in cleartext to long-term storage. That includes any replicated backups.
2) For zero-retention mode, can you confirm: are ephemeral caches ever snapshotted to disk during maintenance or crash recovery? We need an assurance against that.
3) Sample logs: attached a tiny sample (labsignal-sample-logs.txt) — it contains two anonymized sessions. For each session the fields we consider sensitive are marked with [PII].

On the short-term debug window: 48 hours is reasonable, but we’d like: (a) audit entries listing who accessed the logs, (b) a way to revoke access immediately, and (c) crypto-at-rest key management that keeps keys in our KMS if possible.

Ravi — can you review the sample and comment on anything else we need from Redwood?

Best,
Emma
Head of Product
Labsignal
---
Attachment: labsignal-sample-logs.txt (2 sessions, anonymized)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhou <emma@labsignal.ai>, Ravi Patel <legal@labsignal.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call next steps — confidential logs, locality & TTL

Emma — appreciate the sample and the PII annotations, that’s exactly what we needed. Quick responses inline below and a concrete ask for the legal thread: 

1) Cleartext guarantees: we will never persist annotated PII fields to long-term object storage or backups. Our masking pipeline runs before any write. We’ll provide a short technical note that describes the pipeline and the masking rules (will share with your SecOps).

2) Ephemeral caches and crash-safety: our runtime keeps KV cache in-memory by default. For customers who require it, we do not enable periodic snapshots of in-memory caches. For maintenance windows where snapshots are required, those are opt-in and can be disabled for your tenant. I’ll have an engineering sign-off on this in the DPA addendum.

3) Short-term debug window controls: happy to provide:
   - Audit trail that logs access (user, timestamp, reason).
   - Role-based access with immediate revocation.
   - Customer KMS option: we support bringing-your-own-KMS for encryption at rest in our Private deployment; for Hosted accounts we can integrate with customer KMS in selected regions (EU regions supported).

Action for legal: Marissa — can you draft a minimal addendum that covers (a) 48-hour debug window with automatic deletion and audit logging, (b) explicit EU-only storage commitments for retained artifacts, and (c) statement about in-memory-only KV caches unless explicitly enabled? I’ll include a short technical appendix for SecOps.

Emma/Ravi — assuming the addendum looks good, we can enable a trial 48-hour window for one route (your ingestion endpoint) under the DPA addendum. That will let your engineers validate the revocation and audit flows without broader exposure.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min legal review for next Tue/Wed and loop in Eng if needed.

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call next steps — confidential logs, locality & TTL

Thanks all — quick internal note: I’ll draft the concise DPA addendum this afternoon and include the engineering sign-offs Karthik requested. Sean, please prepare the KMS integration options (hosted + private) and a short runbook for the 48-hour debug lifecycle (provisioning, audit, revocation, deletion proof).

Emma/Ravi — expect the addendum + tech appendix in your inbox by EOD tomorrow. If that timeline is tight for legal, tell us which pieces you need first and we can surface them separately.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
